-- | Reserved name blocks, and linking of independently checked scopes.
--   
--   Each unit of a module system allocates its names inside its own
--   reservation (a <a>NameRange</a>, via <a>withFreshIn</a>), so that
--   units checked independently can be linked afterwards without renaming.
--   <a>ExtWithin</a> is the evidence for that: scope <tt>l</tt> extends
--   scope <tt>n</tt> only within a set of reserved ranges. Note that the
--   ranges bound the <i>extension</i> and not the scope, so the names of
--   <tt>n</tt> itself (typically, a unit's imports) may lie anywhere.
--   
--   Two units that extend a common scope within disjoint reservations have
--   disjoint extensions. <a>withDisjointUnion</a> links them by comparing
--   the reservations rather than the scopes, and hands the continuation
--   the extension evidence for both sides, a <a>ScopeUnion</a> witness
--   that the result is the union and nothing more, and the union's own
--   evidence, so that a linked unit is itself linkable. Evidence composes
--   along a chain of units with <a>composeExtWithin</a>. To link more than
--   two units, or to re-attach a unit loaded from a cache, rebuild the
--   union scope and mint the evidence again with <a>checkExtScope</a> and
--   <a>checkScopeUnion</a>.
--   
--   <a>checkExtScope</a> and <a>checkScopeUnion</a> are a trust boundary.
--   They compare raw names across independently built scopes, which is
--   meaningful only under a deterministic reservation policy. Everything
--   else in this module either tests what it claims or constructs it.
module Control.Monad.Foil.Blocks

-- | Evidence that scope <tt>l</tt> extends scope <tt>n</tt> only within a
--   set of reserved ranges: every name of <tt>l</tt> that is not a name of
--   <tt>n</tt> lies inside one of them.
--   
--   The evidence is built alongside allocation, with <a>extWithinRefl</a>
--   at the start of a unit and <a>extWithinStep</a> at each binder, and
--   composes along a chain of scopes with <a>composeExtWithin</a>. Its
--   runtime content is the ranges, sorted and disjoint.
data ExtWithin (n :: S) (l :: S)

-- | The reservations an <a>ExtWithin</a> is evidence about: sorted,
--   disjoint, adjacent ranges coalesced, empty ones dropped.
extWithinRanges :: forall (n :: S) (l :: S). ExtWithin n l -> [NameRange]

-- | A scope extends itself within any range: the extension is empty.
--   
--   Note that this does <i>not</i> say the range is disjoint from the
--   scope. It is <a>withExtendScopeRange</a> that checks that, because it
--   allocates blindly.
extWithinRefl :: forall (n :: S). NameRange -> ExtWithin n n

-- | Extend the evidence across one more binder, if its name lies inside
--   one of the ranges. One membership test per range.
--   
--   A binder allocated by <a>withFreshIn</a> at one of these ranges always
--   passes. A binder allocated elsewhere, by <a>withFresh</a> or
--   <a>withRefreshed</a>, is rejected with <a>Nothing</a> unless it
--   happens to land inside them, so the evidence cannot be extended past a
--   name that escapes the reservations.
--   
--   <pre>
--   &gt;&gt;&gt; let range = NameRange 100 199
--   
--   &gt;&gt;&gt; withFreshIn range emptyScope (\b -&gt; fmap extWithinRanges (extWithinStep b (extWithinRefl range)))
--   Just [NameRange {nameRangeLo = 100, nameRangeHi = 199}]
--   </pre>
extWithinStep :: forall (l :: S) (l' :: S) (n :: S). NameBinder l l' -> ExtWithin n l -> Maybe (ExtWithin n l')

-- | Compose evidence along a chain of scopes: if <tt>m</tt> extends
--   <tt>n</tt> only within one set of ranges and <tt>l</tt> extends
--   <tt>m</tt> only within another, then <tt>l</tt> extends <tt>n</tt>
--   only within their union.
--   
--   The bound is the union of the two sets and not their hull, so a
--   reservation lying between them stays linkable. Adjacent ranges are
--   coalesced, so a chain of units with consecutive stripes collapses back
--   to a single range.
--   
--   <pre>
--   &gt;&gt;&gt; extWithinRanges (composeExtWithin (extWithinRefl (NameRange 0 9)) (extWithinRefl (NameRange 30 39)))
--   [NameRange {nameRangeLo = 0, nameRangeHi = 9},NameRange {nameRangeLo = 30, nameRangeHi = 39}]
--   
--   &gt;&gt;&gt; extWithinRanges (composeExtWithin (extWithinRefl (NameRange 0 9)) (extWithinRefl (NameRange 10 19)))
--   [NameRange {nameRangeLo = 0, nameRangeHi = 19}]
--   </pre>
composeExtWithin :: forall (n :: S) (m :: S) (l :: S). ExtWithin n m -> ExtWithin m l -> ExtWithin n l

-- | A reservation in use: the range fresh names are allocated from, paired
--   with the evidence that everything allocated since the base scope
--   <tt>c</tt> lies within the unit's ranges.
--   
--   The allocation range is always among the evidence's ranges, so
--   stepping the evidence at a freshly allocated name cannot fail and
--   <a>withFreshInBlock</a> is total. The two components are not
--   redundant: the evidence is a normalised set bounding the whole
--   extension, and once units are composed the range to allocate from can
--   no longer be read off it.
data Block (c :: S) (l :: S)

-- | Start a unit: no names allocated yet, so the evidence is trivial.
beginBlock :: forall (c :: S). NameRange -> Block c c

-- | Resume allocating from a range once the evidence has grown past what a
--   <a>Block</a> tracked by itself, after composing in a loaded unit's
--   evidence with <a>composeExtWithin</a>. This is what lets an
--   interactive unit keep allocating in its own reservation over the
--   enlarged scope.
--   
--   The allocation range must lie inside one of the evidence's ranges. The
--   ranges are normalised, so covering is containment in a single one, and
--   <a>Nothing</a> says the range is not covered.
--   
--   <pre>
--   &gt;&gt;&gt; let grown = composeExtWithin (extWithinRefl (NameRange 0 9)) (extWithinRefl (NameRange 10 19))
--   
--   &gt;&gt;&gt; fmap blockRange (resumeBlock (NameRange 0 9) grown)
--   Just (NameRange {nameRangeLo = 0, nameRangeHi = 9})
--   
--   &gt;&gt;&gt; fmap blockRange (resumeBlock (NameRange 30 39) grown)
--   Nothing
--   </pre>
resumeBlock :: forall (c :: S) (l :: S). NameRange -> ExtWithin c l -> Maybe (Block c l)

-- | The range <a>withFreshInBlock</a> allocates from.
blockRange :: forall (c :: S) (l :: S). Block c l -> NameRange

-- | The evidence accumulated so far: what a finished unit hands to
--   <a>withDisjointUnion</a>, or to <a>composeExtWithin</a> for the next
--   unit of a chain.
blockExt :: forall (c :: S) (l :: S). Block c l -> ExtWithin c l

-- | Allocate a fresh name in the block's range, stepping the evidence in
--   the same motion. Fails with <a>error</a> only on an exhausted range,
--   exactly as <a>withFreshIn</a> does.
--   
--   <pre>
--   &gt;&gt;&gt; withFreshInBlock (beginBlock (NameRange 7 9)) emptyScope (\b block -&gt; (nameId (nameOf b), extWithinRanges (blockExt block)))
--   (7,[NameRange {nameRangeLo = 7, nameRangeHi = 9}])
--   </pre>
withFreshInBlock :: forall (l :: S) (c :: S) r. Distinct l => Block c l -> Scope l -> (forall (l' :: S). DExt l l' => NameBinder l l' -> Block c l' -> r) -> r

-- | Extend a scope with the first <tt>k</tt> names of a range, in one
--   step.
--   
--   This is the bulk form of a unit's allocation, for loading a cached
--   unit whose extension is known to be <tt>k</tt> consecutive names, or
--   for pre-allocating a unit's names before checking its bodies. The
--   range part of the scope must be empty, which is checked, so the
--   extension is fresh by construction. <a>Nothing</a> reports an occupied
--   range, and also a range with fewer than <tt>k</tt> names.
--   
--   The continuation receives the extended scope, the binders in ascending
--   order (for extending a <a>NameMap</a> in the same step), and the
--   <a>ExtWithin</a> evidence. The scope extension is a dense
--   <a>fromRange</a>, &lt;math&gt;.
--   
--   <pre>
--   &gt;&gt;&gt; withExtendScopeRange emptyScope (NameRange 100 199) 3 (\_ binders _ -&gt; rawNameBinderList binders)
--   Just [100,101,102]
--   </pre>
withExtendScopeRange :: forall (c :: S) r. Distinct c => Scope c -> NameRange -> Int -> (forall (n :: S). DExt c n => Scope n -> NameBinderList c n -> ExtWithin c n -> r) -> Maybe r

-- | Evidence that scope <tt>k</tt> is <i>precisely</i> the union of scopes
--   <tt>n</tt> and <tt>m</tt>: every name of <tt>n</tt> and of <tt>m</tt>
--   is a name of <tt>k</tt>, and nothing else is.
--   
--   The extension constraints <tt>(<a>Ext</a> n k, <a>Ext</a> m k)</tt>
--   state only the first half, since a strict superset of the union
--   satisfies them too. The second half is what totality of a merged
--   <a>NameMap</a> rests on, so <a>unionNameMaps</a> demands this witness.
--   It comes from <a>withDisjointUnion</a>, which builds the union, or
--   from <a>checkScopeUnion</a>, which tests for it.
data ScopeUnion (n :: S) (m :: S) (k :: S)

-- | Link two scopes that extend a common scope <tt>c</tt> within their
--   respective reservations. The evidence check is one sweep over the two
--   range sets; the scope union is one <a>union</a>.
--   
--   <a>Nothing</a> when the two range sets overlap. The test is soundness
--   and not an optimisation. The extensions <tt>n \ c</tt> and <tt>m \
--   c</tt> lie inside their respective range sets, so their disjointness
--   is what guarantees that no raw name denotes two different variables in
--   the union. The names the two scopes share are exactly the names of
--   <tt>c</tt>, identified rather than renamed apart, which is what
--   linking two units over a common import must do.
--   
--   The continuation receives both extension facts at once, a
--   <a>ScopeUnion</a> witness (which <a>unionNameMaps</a> requires), and
--   the union's own <a>ExtWithin</a>, so that a linked unit is itself
--   linkable and a whole build folds through this one function. It also
--   receives <tt><a>Ext</a> c k</tt>, which a caller cannot derive on the
--   spot.
withDisjointUnion :: forall (c :: S) (n :: S) (m :: S) r. (Distinct n, Distinct m) => ExtWithin c n -> ExtWithin c m -> Scope n -> Scope m -> (forall (k :: S). (Ext n k, Ext m k, Ext c k, Distinct k) => Scope k -> ScopeUnion n m k -> ExtWithin c k -> r) -> Maybe r

-- | Test that a scope is precisely the union of two others, and produce
--   the witness if so. &lt;math&gt;.
--   
--   This is the union witness for the re-attachment path, where the union
--   scope was rebuilt rather than handed down by <a>withDisjointUnion</a>.
--   Like <a>checkExtScope</a>, it compares raw names across independently
--   built scopes, and is meaningful only under a deterministic reservation
--   policy.
checkScopeUnion :: forall (n :: S) (m :: S) (k :: S). Scope n -> Scope m -> Scope k -> Maybe (ScopeUnion n m k)

-- | Test that every name of one scope is a name of another, and mint the
--   extension evidence if so. &lt;math&gt; (<a>isSubsetOf</a>).
--   
--   <b>This is a trust boundary.</b> The test compares raw names, and raw
--   names from independently built scopes need not mean the same variable.
--   The type system tracks meaning through binders, and this function goes
--   around it deliberately, to re-attach a scope built elsewhere: in an
--   earlier run, in a cache, or in a parallel session. It is sound only
--   under the external discipline that a raw name has one global meaning,
--   which a deterministic reservation policy provides. Nothing here checks
--   that discipline, and the caller's allocator is what has to.
checkExtScope :: forall (n :: S) (l :: S). Scope n -> Scope l -> Maybe (ExtEvidence n l)

-- | Union of two total maps into a map on the union of their scopes.
--   Left-biased, like <a>union</a>.
--   
--   The witness is what makes the result total on <tt>k</tt>. The inputs
--   are total on <tt>n</tt> and <tt>m</tt>, and <a>ScopeUnion</a> says
--   that <tt>k</tt> holds their names and no others. (It also determines
--   <tt>k</tt>, which an extension constraint alone would leave open.)
--   
--   What no witness can say is that the two maps agree on the names their
--   scopes share. Linked units agree there when the shared part comes from
--   the same checked imports, and the left bias then only ever chooses
--   between equal entries.
unionNameMaps :: forall (n :: S) (m :: S) (k :: S) a. ScopeUnion n m k -> NameMap n a -> NameMap m a -> NameMap k a


-- | Main definitions of the foil that can be reused for specific
--   implementations.
--   
--   The original description of this approach is described in the IFL 2022
--   paper by Maclaurin, Radul, and Paszke <a>«The Foil: Capture-Avoiding
--   Substitution With No Sharp Edges»</a>. This module also introduces
--   <a>CoSinkable</a> class, generalizing handling of patterns, as
--   described in <a>«Free Foil: Generating Efficient and Scope-Safe
--   Abstract Syntax»</a>.
--   
--   Since the representation of scopes and substitutions is either
--   <tt>IntMap</tt> or <tt>IntSet</tt>, many of the operations have a
--   worst-case complexity of &lt;math&gt;. This means that the operation
--   can become linear in the size of the scope &lt;math&gt; with a maximum
--   of &lt;math&gt;, the number of bits in an <a>Int</a> (32 or 64).
module Control.Monad.Foil

-- | <a>S</a> is a data kind of scope indices.
data S

-- | <a>VoidS</a> is the only explicit scope available to the users,
--   representing an empty scope. All other scopes are represented with
--   type variables, bound in rank-2 polymophic functions like
--   <a>withFreshBinder</a>.
VoidS :: S

-- | A safe scope, indexed by a type-level scope index <tt>n</tt>.
data Scope (n :: S)

-- | A name in a safe scope, indexed by a type-level scope index
--   <tt>n</tt>.
data Name (n :: S)

-- | A name binder is a name that extends scope <tt>n</tt> to a (larger)
--   scope <tt>l</tt>.
data NameBinder (n :: S) (l :: S)

-- | An empty scope (without any names).
emptyScope :: Scope 'VoidS

-- | &lt;math&gt;. Extend a scope with one name (safely). Note that as long
--   as the foil is used as intended, the name binder is guaranteed to
--   introduce a name that does not appear in the initial scope.
extendScope :: forall (n :: S) (l :: S). NameBinder n l -> Scope n -> Scope l

-- | Extend scope with variables inside a pattern. This is a more flexible
--   version of <a>extendScope</a>.
extendScopePattern :: forall (n :: S) pattern (l :: S). (Distinct n, CoSinkable pattern) => pattern n l -> Scope n -> Scope l

-- | A runtime check for potential name capture.
member :: forall (l :: S) (n :: S). Name l -> Scope n -> Bool

-- | Extract name from a name binder.
nameOf :: forall (n :: S) (l :: S). NameBinder n l -> Name l

-- | Extract names from a pattern. This is a more flexible version of
--   <a>nameOf</a>.
namesOfPattern :: forall pattern (n :: S) (l :: S). (Distinct n, CoSinkable pattern) => pattern n l -> [Name l]

-- | Convert <a>Name</a> into an identifier. This may be useful for
--   printing and debugging.
nameId :: forall (l :: S). Name l -> Id

-- | We will use <a>Int</a> for efficient representation of identifiers.
type Id = Int

-- | Raw name is simply an identifier.
type RawName = Id

-- | Allocate a fresh binder for a given scope.
withFreshBinder :: forall (n :: S) r. Scope n -> (forall (l :: S). () => NameBinder n l -> r) -> r

-- | Safely produce a fresh name binder with respect to a given scope.
withFresh :: forall (n :: S) r. Distinct n => Scope n -> (forall (l :: S). DExt n l => NameBinder n l -> r) -> r

-- | An inclusive reservation of a contiguous range of raw names.
--   
--   A range is a bound on an allocator (see <a>withFreshIn</a>), not a set
--   of names: its runtime content is two <a>Int</a>s. A range with <tt>lo
--   &gt; hi</tt> is empty.
data NameRange
NameRange :: !RawName -> !RawName -> NameRange

-- | The smallest name of the reservation.
[nameRangeLo] :: NameRange -> !RawName

-- | The largest name of the reservation (inclusive).
[nameRangeHi] :: NameRange -> !RawName

-- | The range of all non-negative names.
--   
--   On a scope without negative members, allocation within
--   <a>fullNameRange</a> agrees with <a>rawFreshName</a>. The two diverge
--   on a scope with negative members: <a>rawFreshName</a> allocates right
--   above the maximum, wherever that lands, while <a>fullNameRange</a>
--   clamps allocation to non-negative names.
fullNameRange :: NameRange

-- | Safely produce a fresh name binder, allocated within a given range.
--   
--   The binder is fresh with respect to the whole ambient scope, not
--   merely to its part inside the range. Indeed, the allocated name lies
--   in the range and is greater than every scope member there, while a
--   scope member outside the range cannot be equal to a name inside it
--   (see <a>rawFreshNameIn</a>). Thus the usual freshness evidence
--   applies, and no invariant beyond the scope itself is required.
--   
--   This is the primitive behind allocation policies such as per-module
--   name blocks: reserve disjoint ranges for independently checked units,
--   and the names allocated for them can never collide.
--   
--   Fails with <a>error</a> when the range is exhausted. Use
--   <a>tryWithFreshIn</a> to handle exhaustion instead.
--   
--   <pre>
--   &gt;&gt;&gt; withFreshIn (NameRange 100 199) emptyScope (nameId . nameOf)
--   100
--   </pre>
withFreshIn :: forall (n :: S) r. Distinct n => NameRange -> Scope n -> (forall (l :: S). DExt n l => NameBinder n l -> r) -> r

-- | A version of <a>withFreshIn</a> that reports an exhausted range with
--   <a>Nothing</a> instead of failing. A driver that hands out ranges can
--   then report which unit ran out of its reservation.
tryWithFreshIn :: forall (n :: S) r. Distinct n => NameRange -> Scope n -> (forall (l :: S). DExt n l => NameBinder n l -> r) -> Maybe r

-- | Rename a given pattern into a fresh version of it to extend a given
--   scope.
--   
--   This is similar to <a>withRefreshedPattern</a>, except here renaming
--   always takes place.
withFreshPattern :: forall (o :: S) pattern (e :: S -> Type) (n :: S) (l :: S) r. (Distinct o, CoSinkable pattern, Sinkable e, InjectName e) => Scope o -> pattern n l -> (forall (o' :: S). DExt o o' => (Substitution e n o -> Substitution e l o') -> pattern o o' -> Scope o' -> r) -> r

-- | Safely rename (if necessary) a given name to extend a given scope.
--   This is similar to <a>withFresh</a>, except if the name does not clash
--   with the scope, it can be used immediately, without renaming.
withRefreshed :: forall (o :: S) (i :: S) r. Distinct o => Scope o -> Name i -> (forall (o' :: S). DExt o o' => NameBinder o o' -> r) -> r

-- | A version of <a>withRefreshed</a> that allocates the replacement name
--   within a given range when the candidate is taken. A client that
--   reserves regions of the raw-name line (per-module stripes, a region
--   for locals) uses this so that a rename cannot stray into someone
--   else's reservation.
withRefreshedIn :: forall (o :: S) (i :: S) r. Distinct o => NameRange -> Scope o -> Name i -> (forall (o' :: S). DExt o o' => NameBinder o o' -> r) -> r

-- | Safely rename (if necessary) a given pattern to extend a given scope.
--   This is similar to <a>withFreshPattern</a>, except if a name in the
--   pattern does not clash with the scope, it can be used immediately,
--   without renaming.
--   
--   This is a more general version of <a>withRefreshed</a>.
--   
--   The continuation also receives the scope extended with the refreshed
--   pattern: the traversal computes it along the way, so the caller does
--   not recompute it with <a>extendScopePattern</a> (a second traversal of
--   the same pattern). The same holds for <a>withFreshPattern</a> and
--   <a>withRefreshedPattern'</a>.
--   
--   Note that there is deliberately no fast path for the case when
--   <i>every</i> binder of the pattern is already fresh in the ambient
--   scope. It is tempting to test all binders at once and, when none
--   clashes, hand the continuation <tt>sink</tt> instead of a renaming
--   composed per binder. That would be unsound.
--   
--   Even when a binder is not renamed, the per-binder step is not the
--   identity: <a>addRename</a> <i>deletes</i> the name from the
--   substitution, which is how the binder shadows an outer binding of the
--   same raw name. For skipping that delete to be harmless we would need
--   the substitution's domain to avoid the pattern's binder names, but the
--   substitution's domain lives in the pattern's own scope <tt>n</tt>,
--   while freshness is tested against the unrelated ambient scope
--   <tt>o</tt>.
--   
--   The two can indeed disagree, because <a>sink</a> is a coercion and
--   does not rename: a term built in a small scope keeps its binder names
--   when it is placed in a larger one, so a binder can share a raw name
--   with its own enclosing scope. Ordinary evaluation produces such terms,
--   with a <tt>λ x1</tt> nested inside another <tt>λ x1</tt>. Handing such
--   a caller <tt>sink</tt> would apply its substitution to a name the
--   pattern binds, which is to say capture the bound variable.
withRefreshedPattern :: forall (o :: S) pattern (e :: S -> Type) (n :: S) (l :: S) r. (Distinct o, CoSinkable pattern, Sinkable e, InjectName e) => Scope o -> pattern n l -> (forall (o' :: S). DExt o o' => (Substitution e n o -> Substitution e l o') -> pattern o o' -> Scope o' -> r) -> r

-- | Refresh (if needed) bound variables introduced in a pattern.
--   
--   This is a version of <a>withRefreshedPattern</a> that uses functional
--   renamings instead of <a>Substitution</a>.
--   
--   Like <a>withRefreshedPattern</a>, this has no
--   all-binders-already-fresh fast path, and for the same reason. Here
--   shadowing is handled by <a>unsinkName</a> rather than by a delete: a
--   name the pattern binds is routed to <a>injectName</a> and never
--   reaches the caller's renaming, whether or not the binder was
--   refreshed.
withRefreshedPattern' :: forall pattern (o :: S) e (n :: S) (l :: S) r. (CoSinkable pattern, Distinct o, InjectName e, Sinkable e) => Scope o -> pattern n l -> (forall (o' :: S). DExt o o' => ((Name n -> e o) -> Name l -> e o') -> pattern o o' -> Scope o' -> r) -> r

-- | Try coercing the name back to the (smaller) scope, given a binder that
--   extends that scope.
unsinkName :: forall (n :: S) (l :: S). NameBinder n l -> Name l -> Maybe (Name n)

-- | Check if a name in the extended context is introduced in a pattern or
--   comes from the outer scope <tt>n</tt>.
--   
--   This is a generalization of <a>unsinkName</a>.
unsinkNamePattern :: forall pattern (n :: S) (l :: S). (Distinct n, CoSinkable pattern) => pattern n l -> Name l -> Maybe (Name n)

-- | A set of names of scope <tt>n</tt>.
--   
--   This is not a <a>Scope</a>: a <a>Scope</a> is <i>all</i> the names in
--   scope, and the foil relies on that (it is what freshness is tested
--   against, and what <a>Distinct</a> speaks about). A <a>NameSet</a> is
--   any subset of them, such as the names a term uses or the assumptions a
--   declaration depends on, and carries no such invariant.
--   
--   <a>&lt;&gt;</a> is union and <a>mempty</a> is empty, so a
--   <a>NameSet</a> can be accumulated with <a>foldMap</a>.
data NameSet (n :: S)

-- | An empty set of names.
emptyNameSet :: forall (n :: S). NameSet n

-- | &lt;math&gt;. A set of one name.
nameSetSingleton :: forall (n :: S). Name n -> NameSet n

-- | &lt;math&gt;. Add a name to a set.
nameSetInsert :: forall (n :: S). Name n -> NameSet n -> NameSet n

-- | &lt;math&gt;. Is this name in the set?
nameSetMember :: forall (n :: S). Name n -> NameSet n -> Bool

-- | Is the set empty?
nameSetNull :: forall (n :: S). NameSet n -> Bool

-- | How many names are in the set?
nameSetSize :: forall (n :: S). NameSet n -> Int

-- | The names in the set, in ascending order of their identifiers.
nameSetToList :: forall (n :: S). NameSet n -> [Name n]

-- | A set of the given names.
nameSetFromList :: forall (n :: S). [Name n] -> NameSet n

-- | The names a pattern binds.
nameSetOfPattern :: forall binder (n :: S) (l :: S). CoSinkable binder => binder n l -> NameSet l

-- | All the names in a scope.
scopeToNameSet :: forall (n :: S). Scope n -> NameSet n

-- | &lt;math&gt;. Does the scope contain every name in the set?
--   
--   This is the test that restriction of a term comes down to, so it is
--   the one place a restriction is paid for: compare a term's support
--   against the scope it is to be restricted to.
nameSetSubsetOfScope :: forall (l :: S) (n :: S). NameSet l -> Scope n -> Bool

-- | Drop the names a pattern binds, taking a set of names of the inner
--   scope to a set of names of the outer one.
--   
--   This is <a>unsinkNamePattern</a> for a whole set at once, and
--   &lt;math&gt; rather than one membership test per name. Removing the
--   pattern's names is right even when one of them shares a raw name with
--   the enclosing scope: inside the pattern that raw name denotes the
--   binder, so no occurrence of it there is an occurrence of the outer
--   name.
unsinkNameSet :: forall binder (n :: S) (l :: S). CoSinkable binder => binder n l -> NameSet l -> NameSet n

-- | Cut a scope down to a subset of its names.
--   
--   The names must be names of <tt>n</tt>; nothing checks it, which is why
--   this is the only entry point and takes a <a>NameSet</a> rather than a
--   bare <tt>IntSet</tt>. The continuation gets <tt><a>Ext</a> m n</tt>,
--   so anything living in the smaller scope can be <a>sink</a>ed back into
--   the larger one for free, and <tt><a>Distinct</a> m</tt>, since a
--   subset of distinct names is distinct.
--   
--   <b>Note on allocation.</b> A name allocated from the restricted scope
--   is fresh with respect to <tt>m</tt> and <i>not</i> to <tt>n</tt>, so
--   it may collide with a name of <tt>n</tt> that the restriction dropped.
--   This is sound, since <tt><a>Ext</a> m n</tt> gives no way to move a
--   term of <tt>n</tt> into a scope extending <tt>m</tt>. It does mean
--   that a restricted scope is for inspecting and restricting terms, and
--   not a base to build new binders on and then mix with the original
--   scope.
withRestrictedScope :: forall (n :: S) r. Distinct n => NameSet n -> (forall (m :: S). (Ext m n, Distinct m) => Scope m -> r) -> r

-- | <a>Sinkable</a> for a type with any number of scope indices, and the
--   class a pattern derives to obtain the foil's traversals. An instance
--   is normally empty, leaving the generic implementation to walk the
--   <a>RepK</a> of the type.
class SinkableK (f :: S -> k)

-- | Rename every scope index of a value, in continuation-passing style.
sinkabilityProofK :: forall (as :: LoT (S -> k)) (bs :: LoT (S -> k)) r. SinkableK f => RenamingsK as bs -> (f :@@: as) -> (forall (cs :: LoT (S -> k)). () => RenamingsK as cs -> (f :@@: cs) -> r) -> r
($dmsinkabilityProofK) :: forall (as :: LoT (S -> k)) (bs :: LoT (S -> k)) r. (SinkableK f, GenericK f, GSinkableK (RepK f)) => RenamingsK as bs -> (f :@@: as) -> (forall (cs :: LoT (S -> k)). () => RenamingsK as cs -> (f :@@: cs) -> r) -> r

-- | Sinking an expression from scope <tt>n</tt> into a (usualy extended)
--   scope <tt>l</tt>, given the renaming (injection from scope <tt>n</tt>
--   to scope <tt>l</tt>).
class Sinkable (e :: S -> Type)

-- | An implementation of this method that typechecks proves to the
--   compiler that the expression is indeed <a>Sinkable</a>. However,
--   instead of this implementation, <a>sink</a> should be used at all call
--   sites for efficiency.
sinkabilityProof :: forall (n :: S) (l :: S). Sinkable e => (Name n -> Name l) -> e n -> e l
($dmsinkabilityProof) :: forall (n :: S) (l :: S). (Sinkable e, GenericK e, GSinkableK (RepK e)) => (Name n -> Name l) -> e n -> e l

-- | <a>CoSinkable</a> is to patterns (generalized binders) what
--   <a>Sinkable</a> is to expressions.
--   
--   See Section 2.3 of <a>«Free Foil: Generating Efficient and Scope-Safe
--   Abstract Syntax»</a> for more details.
class CoSinkable (pattern :: S -> S -> Type)

-- | An implementation of this method that typechecks proves to the
--   compiler that the pattern is indeed <a>CoSinkable</a>. However,
--   instead of this implementation, <a>extendRenaming</a> should be used
--   at all call sites for efficiency.
coSinkabilityProof :: forall (n :: S) (n' :: S) (l :: S) r. CoSinkable pattern => (Name n -> Name n') -> pattern n l -> (forall (l' :: S). () => (Name l -> Name l') -> pattern n' l' -> r) -> r
($dmcoSinkabilityProof) :: forall (n :: S) (n' :: S) (l :: S) r. (CoSinkable pattern, GenericK pattern, GSinkableK (RepK pattern)) => (Name n -> Name n') -> pattern n l -> (forall (l' :: S). () => (Name l -> Name l') -> pattern n' l' -> r) -> r

-- | Generalized processing of a pattern.
--   
--   You can see <a>withPattern</a> as a CPS-style traversal over the
--   binders in a pattern.
--   
--   <h2>Patterns that carry scoped payloads</h2>
--   
--   Note that the ambient scope <tt>o</tt> and the pattern's own scope
--   <tt>n</tt> are unrelated: <a>nameBinderListOf</a> passes
--   <a>emptyScope</a> and <a>namesOfPattern</a> passes no scope at all.
--   The only thing relating the two is the pair of binders each step of
--   the traversal produces, the one the pattern has and the one the
--   callback hands back.
--   
--   A pattern whose fields are all binders and plain data does not notice
--   this, and can take the default implementation. A pattern carrying a
--   field indexed by <i>its own scope</i>, such as the type of a
--   telescope's step, does notice: to rebuild that field at <tt>o</tt> it
--   needs a renaming, and the only honest one is the identity on the raw
--   names the pattern does not bind, corrected at the binders that were
--   refreshed. That renaming is <a>PatternTransport</a>, and such a
--   pattern should implement <a>withPattern</a> by hand, threading one
--   through the traversal. See <a>transportPayload</a> for the whole
--   recipe.
--   
--   The default implementation cannot do this, since it goes through
--   <a>unsafeSetNameBinders</a>, which replaces the binders and leaves
--   every other field as it stands: a payload mentioning a refreshed
--   binder would keep the name that binder used to have. Rather than
--   answer wrongly, it refuses: a field indexed by a scope is a type error
--   in the generic implementation, naming the field and pointing here.
withPattern :: forall (o :: S) f (n :: S) (l :: S) r. (CoSinkable pattern, Distinct o) => (forall (x :: S) (y :: S) (z :: S) r'. Distinct z => Scope z -> NameBinder x y -> (forall (z' :: S). DExt z z' => f x y z z' -> NameBinder z z' -> r') -> r') -> (forall (x :: S) (z :: S) (z' :: S). DExt z z' => f x x z z') -> (forall (x :: S) (y :: S) (y' :: S) (z :: S) (z' :: S) (z'' :: S). (DExt z z', DExt z' z'') => f x y z z' -> f y y' z' z'' -> f x y' z z'') -> Scope o -> pattern n l -> (forall (o' :: S). DExt o o' => f n l o o' -> pattern o o' -> Scope o' -> r) -> r
($dmwithPattern) :: forall (o :: S) f (n :: S) (l :: S) r. (CoSinkable pattern, Distinct o, GenericK pattern, GValidNameBinders pattern (RepK pattern), GHasNameBinders (RepK pattern)) => (forall (x :: S) (y :: S) (z :: S) r'. Distinct z => Scope z -> NameBinder x y -> (forall (z' :: S). DExt z z' => f x y z z' -> NameBinder z z' -> r') -> r') -> (forall (x :: S) (z :: S) (z' :: S). DExt z z' => f x x z z') -> (forall (x :: S) (y :: S) (y' :: S) (z :: S) (z' :: S) (z'' :: S). (DExt z z', DExt z' z'') => f x y z z' -> f y y' z' z'' -> f x y' z z'') -> Scope o -> pattern n l -> (forall (o' :: S). DExt o o' => f n l o o' -> pattern o o' -> Scope o' -> r) -> r

-- | The renaming that carries a pattern's payloads into the ambient scope
--   of <a>withPattern</a>.
--   
--   A pattern may carry fields indexed by its own scope, the standard
--   example being a telescope, where each step has a type in the scope the
--   steps before it extend to. Rebuilding such a pattern at the ambient
--   scope means rebuilding those fields there too, and <a>withPattern</a>
--   hands the instance no renaming for it. This is that renaming,
--   accumulated as the traversal goes.
--   
--   It is abstract on purpose: the only ways to build one are
--   <a>verbatimTransport</a> and <a>transportUnderBinder</a>, which
--   together are exactly what a correct <a>withPattern</a> does.
--   
--   Soundness rests on what <a>withPattern</a> is allowed to do. It
--   replaces binders and nothing else, so a raw name the pattern does not
--   bind means in <tt>o</tt> what it meant in <tt>n</tt>, and the identity
--   on raw names is a renaming from the one to the other. That is the same
--   coercion <a>extendRenaming</a> and <a>unsafeAssertFresh</a> already
--   perform.
data PatternTransport (n :: S) (o :: S)

-- | The transport to start a <a>withPattern</a> traversal with, before any
--   binder has been seen.
verbatimTransport :: forall (n :: S) (o :: S). PatternTransport n o

-- | Extend a transport by one binder of the pattern.
--   
--   The names of the inner scope are the binder's own, which goes to
--   whatever the refreshed binder introduces, and the names of the outer
--   scope, which the transport so far already answers for.
transportUnderBinder :: forall (n :: S) (o :: S) (i :: S) (o' :: S). PatternTransport n o -> NameBinder n i -> NameBinder o o' -> PatternTransport i o'

-- | Carry a payload along a transport.
--   
--   The <a>Sinkable</a> instance does the walking, and only when it has
--   to. While no binder has been refreshed the payload is taken over as it
--   stands, so the traversals that never rename
--   (<a>extendScopePattern</a>, <a>namesOfPattern</a>,
--   <a>nameBinderListOf</a>) do not walk payloads at all.
--   
--   The whole recipe for a payload-carrying pattern, at a telescope of
--   labelled steps:
--   
--   <pre>
--   instance Sinkable e =&gt; CoSinkable (Telescope label e) where
--     withPattern withBinder unit comp = go verbatimTransport
--       where
--         go _transport _scope TelescopeEmpty cont = cont unit TelescopeEmpty
--         go transport scope (TelescopeCons label payload binder rest) cont =
--           withBinder scope binder $ \fbinder binder' -&gt;
--             go (transportUnderBinder transport binder binder')
--                (extendScope binder' scope) rest $ \frest rest' -&gt;
--               cont (comp fbinder frest)
--                 (TelescopeCons label (transportPayload transport payload)
--                                binder' rest')
--   </pre>
--   
--   Note which transport each payload takes: the one accumulated
--   <i>before</i> its own binder, since that is the scope the payload
--   lives in.
transportPayload :: forall e (n :: S) (o :: S). Sinkable e => PatternTransport n o -> e n -> e o

-- | Carry a single name along a transport.
transportName :: forall (n :: S) (o :: S). PatternTransport n o -> Name n -> Name o

-- | If <tt><a>HasNameBinders</a> f</tt>, then <tt>f n l</tt> is expected
--   to act as a binder, introducing into scope <tt>n</tt> some local
--   variables, extending it to scope <tt>l</tt>. This class allows to
--   extract and modify the set of binders.
class HasNameBinders (f :: S -> S -> Type)

-- | Extract a set of binders from a pattern.
getNameBinders :: forall (n :: S) (l :: S). HasNameBinders f => f n l -> NameBinders n l

-- | Efficient version of <a>sinkabilityProof</a>. In fact, once
--   <a>sinkabilityProof</a> typechecks, it is safe to <a>sink</a> by
--   coercion. See Section 3.5 in <a>«The Foil: Capture-Avoiding
--   Substitution With No Sharp Edges»</a> for the details.
--   
--   <a>sink</a> is the base of a family of &lt;math&gt; coercions, named
--   after <a>Data.Functor.Classes</a>: <a>sink1</a> sinks through one
--   <a>Functor</a> layer and <a>sink2</a> through a <a>Bifunctor</a>, each
--   justified by a lifted sinkability proof of its own.
--   
--   Tuples and records need no private <tt>unsafeCoerce</tt> helpers
--   either. A pair of sinkables is a <a>sink2</a> (<a>Tannen</a> for a
--   whole container of them), and a pair whose first component is
--   scope-free is a <a>sink1</a> through <tt><a>Compose</a> f ((,)
--   a)</tt>. A record of sinkable fields derives <a>Sinkable</a> through
--   <a>deriveGenericK</a> and empty <a>SinkableK</a> and <a>Sinkable</a>
--   instances, after which the whole record sinks in one coercion. A
--   record holding the <a>Scope</a> itself is rightly refused, since there
--   is no <tt>SinkableK Scope</tt>: the scope must grow when a binder is
--   entered, so keep it beside the sinkable part and not inside it.
--   
--   <b>Do not map <a>sink</a> over a container.</b> <tt><a>fmap</a>
--   <a>sink</a></tt> walks the whole spine to apply a per-element
--   coercion, where <a>sink1</a> is one coercion. Rewrite rules turn the
--   elementwise forms into the corresponding family member where they
--   fire, but they are best-effort (they need optimisation on, and
--   <a>fmap</a> at a known functor is often resolved to the instance
--   method first), so write the family member directly.
sink :: forall e (n :: S) (l :: S). (Sinkable e, DExt n l) => e n -> e l

-- | Sink an entire container of sinkable expressions, in &lt;math&gt;:
--   <a>sink</a> lifted through one <a>Functor</a> layer, justified by the
--   <a>Sinkable</a> instance of <a>Compose</a>.
--   
--   The soundness argument for <a>sink</a> extends to a container of
--   sinkables, such as an <a>IntMap</a> of terms, a <a>Map</a> keyed by
--   something else, or a list of them. So there is no need to walk the
--   spine with <tt><a>fmap</a> <a>sink</a></tt>, and entering a binder
--   need not be &lt;math&gt;.
--   
--   <pre>
--   &gt;&gt;&gt; :{
--   sinkEnv :: DExt n l =&gt; Map.Map String (Name n) -&gt; Map.Map String (Name l)
--   sinkEnv = sink1
--   :}
--   </pre>
--   
--   A nested container is one <a>Compose</a> away: <tt>f (g (e n))</tt> is
--   <tt><a>Compose</a> f g (e n)</tt>, and the composition is again a
--   <a>Functor</a>, so <a>sink1</a> covers it too.
--   
--   Two things this does <i>not</i> cover:
--   
--   <ul>
--   <li>A <a>Scope</a> is <b>not</b> sinkable, and must not be sunk: it is
--   the set of names <i>in</i> scope <tt>n</tt>, and it has to grow when a
--   binder is entered (see <a>extendScope</a>).</li>
--   <li>A <a>NameMap</a> must stay <b>total</b> on the names in scope
--   (<a>lookupName</a> errors otherwise), so sinking one has to be paired
--   with adding the new binder's entry (see <a>addNameBinder</a>).</li>
--   </ul>
sink1 :: forall f e (n :: S) (l :: S). (Functor f, Sinkable e, DExt n l) => f (e n) -> f (e l)

-- | Sink both slots of a <a>Bifunctor</a> of sinkables, in &lt;math&gt;,
--   the two scopes moving independently: the shape of <a>liftEq2</a>, with
--   a coercion in place of each of the two functions.
--   
--   <pre>
--   &gt;&gt;&gt; :{
--   sinkBoth :: (DExt n n', DExt m m') =&gt; (Name n, Name m) -&gt; (Name n', Name m')
--   sinkBoth = sink2
--   :}
--   </pre>
--   
--   A container of such pairs is a <a>Bifunctor</a> again, via
--   <a>Tannen</a>, so a list of pairs of names, the shape an α-equivalence
--   test threads, also sinks in one coercion:
--   
--   <pre>
--   &gt;&gt;&gt; :{
--   sinkPairs :: (DExt n n', DExt m m') =&gt; [(Name n, Name m)] -&gt; [(Name n', Name m')]
--   sinkPairs = runTannen . sink2 . Tannen
--   :}
--   </pre>
sink2 :: forall p e1 e2 (n :: S) (n' :: S) (m :: S) (m' :: S). (Bifunctor p, Sinkable e1, Sinkable e2, DExt n n', DExt m m') => p (e1 n) (e2 m) -> p (e1 n') (e2 m')

-- | The sinkability proof lifted through a <a>Bifunctor</a>, with one
--   renaming per slot. Once this typechecks, sinking both slots at once is
--   a coercion; <a>sink2</a> is to this proof exactly what <a>sink</a> is
--   to <a>sinkabilityProof</a>.
sinkabilityProof2 :: forall p e1 e2 (n :: S) (n' :: S) (m :: S) (m' :: S). (Bifunctor p, Sinkable e1, Sinkable e2) => (Name n -> Name n') -> (Name m -> Name m') -> p (e1 n) (e2 m) -> p (e1 n') (e2 m')

-- | The name <a>sink1</a> had before the family existed.

-- | <i>Deprecated: Use sink1, its name in the sink family</i>
sinkContainer :: forall f e (n :: S) (l :: S). (Functor f, Sinkable e, DExt n l) => f (e n) -> f (e l)

-- | Extend renaming when going under a <a>CoSinkable</a> pattern
--   (generalized binder). Note that the scope under pattern is independent
--   of the codomain of the renaming.
--   
--   This function is used to go under binders when implementing
--   <a>sinkabilityProof</a> and is both a generalization of
--   <a>extendRenamingNameBinder</a> and an efficient implementation of
--   <a>coSinkabilityProof</a>.
extendRenaming :: forall pattern (n :: S) (n' :: S) (l :: S) r. CoSinkable pattern => (Name n -> Name n') -> pattern n l -> (forall (l' :: S). () => (Name l -> Name l') -> pattern n' l' -> r) -> r

-- | Extend renaming of binders when going under a <a>CoSinkable</a>
--   pattern (generalized binder). Note that the scope under pattern is
--   independent of the codomain of the renaming.
extendNameBinderRenaming :: forall pattern (i :: S) (n :: S) (n' :: S) (l :: S) r. CoSinkable pattern => (NameBinder i n -> NameBinder i n') -> pattern n l -> (forall (l' :: S). () => (NameBinder n' l -> NameBinder n' l') -> pattern n' l' -> r) -> r

-- | Safely compose renamings of name binders. The underlying
--   implementation is
composeNameBinderRenamings :: forall (n :: S) (i :: S) (i' :: S) (l :: S) (l' :: S). (NameBinder n i -> NameBinder n i') -> (NameBinder i' l -> NameBinder i' l') -> NameBinder n l -> NameBinder n l'

-- | Convert renaming of name binders into renaming of names in the inner
--   scopes.
fromNameBinderRenaming :: forall (n :: S) (l :: S) (l' :: S). (NameBinder n l -> NameBinder n l') -> Name l -> Name l'

-- | Extend renaming when going under a <a>NameBinder</a>. Note that the
--   scope under binder is independent of the codomain of the renaming.
--   
--   Semantically, this function may need to rename the binder (resulting
--   in the new scope <tt>l'</tt>), to make sure it does not clash with
--   scope <tt>n'</tt>. However, as it turns out, the foil makes it safe to
--   implement this function as a coercion. See Appendix A in <a>«The Foil:
--   Capture-Avoiding Substitution With No Sharp Edges»</a> for the
--   details.
--   
--   This function is used to go under binders when implementing
--   <a>sinkabilityProof</a>. A generalization of this function is
--   <a>extendRenaming</a> (which is an efficient version of
--   <a>coSinkabilityProof</a>).
extendRenamingNameBinder :: forall (n :: S) (n' :: S) (l :: S) r. (Name n -> Name n') -> NameBinder n l -> (forall (l' :: S). () => (Name l -> Name l') -> NameBinder n' l' -> r) -> r

-- | A substitution is a mapping from names in scope <tt>i</tt> to
--   expressions <tt>e o</tt> in scope <tt>o</tt>.
data Substitution (e :: S -> Type) (i :: S) (o :: S)

-- | Apply substitution to a given name.
lookupSubst :: forall e (i :: S) (o :: S). InjectName e => Substitution e i o -> Name i -> e o

-- | Identity substitution maps all names to expresion-variables.
identitySubst :: forall (e :: S -> Type) (i :: S). InjectName e => Substitution e i i

-- | Whether a substitution maps every name to itself (see
--   <a>addRename</a>, which deletes identity renames, so this is one null
--   test).
nullSubst :: forall (e :: S -> Type) (i :: S) (o :: S). Substitution e i o -> Bool

-- | An empty substitution from an empty scope.
voidSubst :: forall (e :: S -> Type) (n :: S). Substitution e 'VoidS n

-- | Extend substitution with a particular mapping.
addSubst :: forall e (i :: S) (o :: S) (i' :: S). Substitution e i o -> NameBinder i i' -> e o -> Substitution e i' o

-- | Extend a substitution with a value for each binder of a pattern, in
--   the order the pattern binds them.
addSubstPattern :: forall binder e (i :: S) (o :: S) (i' :: S). CoSinkable binder => Substitution e i o -> binder i i' -> [e o] -> Substitution e i' o

-- | Extend a substitution with a value for each binder of a chain, in
--   order. Fails with <a>error</a> when the list of values is too short.
addSubstList :: forall e (i :: S) (o :: S) (i' :: S). Substitution e i o -> NameBinderList i i' -> [e o] -> Substitution e i' o

-- | Add variable renaming to a substitution.
--   
--   When the binder is mapped to its own name, the name is <i>deleted</i>
--   from the substitution rather than mapped to itself. This is an
--   optimization, but it is not only an optimization: it is also how the
--   binder shadows an outer binding of the same raw name, so the delete
--   cannot be skipped even when nothing is being renamed. See
--   <a>withRefreshedPattern</a> for why that rules out an
--   all-binders-fresh fast path.
addRename :: forall (e :: S -> Type) (i :: S) (o :: S) (i' :: S). InjectName e => Substitution e i o -> NameBinder i i' -> Name o -> Substitution e i' o

-- | Unification result for two binders, extending some common scope to
--   scopes <tt>l</tt> and <tt>r</tt> respectively.
--   
--   Due to the implementation of the foil, we can often rename binders
--   efficiently, by renaming binders only in one of the two unified terms.
data UnifyNameBinders (pattern :: S -> S -> Type) (n :: S) (l :: S) (r :: S)

-- | Binders are the same, proving that type parameters <tt>l</tt> and
--   <tt>r</tt> are in fact equivalent.
[SameNameBinders] :: forall (n :: S) (l :: S) (pattern :: S -> S -> Type). NameBinders n l -> UnifyNameBinders pattern n l l

-- | It is possible to safely rename the left binder to match the right
--   one.
[RenameLeftNameBinder] :: forall (n :: S) (r :: S) (l :: S) (pattern :: S -> S -> Type). NameBinders n r -> (NameBinder n l -> NameBinder n r) -> UnifyNameBinders pattern n l r

-- | It is possible to safely rename the right binder to match the left
--   one.
[RenameRightNameBinder] :: forall (n :: S) (l :: S) (r :: S) (pattern :: S -> S -> Type). NameBinders n l -> (NameBinder n r -> NameBinder n l) -> UnifyNameBinders pattern n l r

-- | It is necessary to rename both binders.
[RenameBothBinders] :: forall (n :: S) (lr :: S) (l :: S) (r :: S) (pattern :: S -> S -> Type). NameBinders n lr -> (NameBinder n l -> NameBinder n lr) -> (NameBinder n r -> NameBinder n lr) -> UnifyNameBinders pattern n l r

-- | Cannot unify to (sub)patterns.
[NotUnifiable] :: forall (pattern :: S -> S -> Type) (n :: S) (l :: S) (r :: S). UnifyNameBinders pattern n l r

-- | Unify binders either by asserting that they are the same, or by
--   providing a <i>safe</i> renaming function to convert one binder to
--   another.
--   
--   When the binders differ, the one with the <i>larger</i> name is
--   renamed towards the one with the smaller name. The direction is
--   deliberate, but it is not what makes the renaming safe.
--   
--   The renaming returned here is not applied by substituting names
--   blindly. Callers push it through a term with <a>liftRM</a>, which
--   refreshes a binder whenever it would capture. So the target name may
--   well be used by a binder <i>inside</i> the term being renamed, and the
--   result is still correct. Binder names do not always grow with depth: a
--   term built in a small scope keeps its small binder names when
--   <a>sink</a> places it in a larger one.
unifyNameBinders :: forall (i :: S) (l :: S) (r :: S) (pattern :: S -> S -> Type). Distinct i => NameBinder i l -> NameBinder i r -> UnifyNameBinders pattern i l r

-- | Chain unification of nested patterns.
andThenUnifyPatterns :: forall pattern (l :: S) (l' :: S) (n :: S) (r :: S) (r' :: S). (UnifiablePattern pattern, Distinct l, Distinct l') => UnifyNameBinders pattern n l l' -> (pattern l r, pattern l' r') -> UnifyNameBinders pattern n r r'

-- | Chain unification of nested patterns with <a>NameBinder</a>s.
andThenUnifyNameBinders :: forall (pattern :: S -> S -> Type) (l :: S) (l' :: S) (n :: S) (r :: S) (r' :: S). (UnifiablePattern pattern, Distinct l, Distinct l') => UnifyNameBinders pattern n l l' -> (NameBinder l r, NameBinder l' r') -> UnifyNameBinders pattern n r r'

-- | A pattern type is unifiable if it is possible to match two patterns
--   and decide how to rename binders.
--   
--   Note that the default implementation compares patterns only up to
--   their binders. See <a>unifyPatterns</a> for what that does and does
--   not distinguish.
class CoSinkable pattern => UnifiablePattern (pattern :: S -> S -> Type)

-- | Unify two patterns and decide which binders need to be renamed.
unifyPatterns :: forall (n :: S) (l :: S) (r :: S). (UnifiablePattern pattern, Distinct n) => pattern n l -> pattern n r -> UnifyNameBinders pattern n l r

-- | The default implementation flattens both patterns to their binders
--   (via <a>nameBinderListOf</a>) and unifies the resulting
--   <a>NameBinderList</a>s. It therefore compares only the <i>number and
--   order</i> of binders, and ignores
--   
--   <ul>
--   <li>the constructor, so two patterns built from <i>different</i>
--   constructors with the same number of binders unify;</li>
--   <li>non-binding fields (locations, sorts, literals), whatever their
--   values;</li>
--   <li>the nesting of sub-patterns, so <tt>(x, (y, z))</tt> unifies with
--   <tt>((x, y), z)</tt>.</li>
--   </ul>
--   
--   For most languages this is the intended notion of α-equivalence: what
--   the body of a binding construct can refer to is precisely the
--   pattern's binders, in order. Since α-equivalence is defined in terms
--   of <a>unifyPatterns</a>, this also means that terms differing only in
--   such a pattern are α-equivalent.
--   
--   A pattern that carries semantically relevant data needs the instance
--   written by hand instead. Use <a>UnifiableInPattern</a> to compare
--   non-binding fields, which also lets an instance ignore some of them
--   deliberately, as a generated instance does for BNFC source positions.
--   
--   A field that is <i>scope-indexed</i>, such as a telescope step's type,
--   cannot be compared here at all, since comparing it up to α needs the
--   ambient scope and this method is given only <a>Distinct</a>. Write
--   <a>unifyPatternsIn</a> for that, and leave this one as the binder-only
--   approximation.
($dmunifyPatterns) :: forall (n :: S) (l :: S) (r :: S). (UnifiablePattern pattern, CoSinkable pattern, Distinct n) => pattern n l -> pattern n r -> UnifyNameBinders pattern n l r

-- | Unify two patterns with the ambient scope at hand.
--   
--   Everything in the library that compares patterns and holds a scope
--   goes through this method, α-equivalence included, so this is the one
--   to implement when the comparison needs a scope. Comparing the payloads
--   of a pattern that carries them does: <a>alphaEquivIn</a> asks for a
--   <a>Scope</a>.
--   
--   Note that the verdict speaks about binders, so an instance comparing
--   payloads has to apply the renaming the verdict prescribes before it
--   compares them, exactly as <a>alphaEquivScoped</a> applies it to the
--   body of a scoped term. Two telescopes <tt>(A : 𝕌) (x : A)</tt> and
--   <tt>(B : 𝕌) (y : B)</tt> are α-equivalent, and their second payloads
--   are only equal once the first binders have been identified.
--   
--   The default ignores the scope and answers with <a>unifyPatterns</a>.
--   An instance that overrides this one should leave <a>unifyPatterns</a>
--   in place as the binder-only approximation rather than remove it. That
--   is what <a>unsafeEqPattern</a> and any caller without a scope will
--   get, and it may be more permissive than this one, never less.
unifyPatternsIn :: forall (n :: S) (l :: S) (r :: S). (UnifiablePattern pattern, Distinct n) => Scope n -> pattern n l -> pattern n r -> UnifyNameBinders pattern n l r

-- | Unification of values in patterns. By default, <a>Eq</a> instance is
--   used, but it may be useful to ignore some data in pattens (such as
--   location annotations).
class UnifiableInPattern a

-- | Unify non-binding components of a pattern.
unifyInPattern :: UnifiableInPattern a => a -> a -> Bool
($dmunifyInPattern) :: (UnifiableInPattern a, Eq a) => a -> a -> Bool

-- | Comparison of scope-indexed values up to α, in a known scope.
--   
--   <a>unifyPatterns</a> is given only <a>Distinct</a>, which is enough to
--   line up binders and not enough to compare anything living in a scope.
--   A pattern that carries a payload needs this to compare its payloads
--   against another's, which is what <a>unifyPatternsIn</a> is for.
class AlphaEquiv (e :: S -> Type)

-- | Are two values of one scope α-equivalent?
alphaEquivIn :: forall (n :: S). (AlphaEquiv e, Distinct n) => Scope n -> e n -> e n -> Bool

-- | An <i>unordered</i> collection of <a>NameBinder</a>s, that together
--   extend scope <tt>n</tt> to scope <tt>l</tt>.
--   
--   For an ordered version see <a>NameBinderList</a>.
data NameBinders (n :: S) (l :: S)

-- | An empty set of binders keeps the scope as is.
emptyNameBinders :: forall (n :: S). NameBinders n n

-- | Composition of sets of binders.
mergeNameBinders :: forall (n :: S) (i :: S) (l :: S). NameBinders n i -> NameBinders i l -> NameBinders n l

-- | An empty pattern type specifies zero possibilities for patterns.
--   
--   This type can be used to specify that patterns are not possible.
data V2 (n :: S) (l :: S)

-- | Since <a>V2</a> values logically don't exist, this witnesses the
--   logical reasoning tool of "ex falso quodlibet".
absurd2 :: forall (n :: S) (l :: S) a. V2 n l -> a

-- | A <i>total</i> map from names in scope <tt>n</tt> to elements of type
--   <tt>a</tt>.
data NameMap (n :: S) a

-- | An empty map belongs in the empty scope.
emptyNameMap :: NameMap 'VoidS a

-- | Map over a <a>NameMap</a>, with the name each value belongs to.
--   
--   This is the keyed version of the derived <a>Functor</a> instance. It
--   cannot change which names the map is defined on, so a map that was
--   total stays total, which is what makes it a safe way to build a
--   <a>Substitution</a> out of one: see <a>nameMapToSubstitution</a>.
mapWithName :: forall (n :: S) a b. (Name n -> a -> b) -> NameMap n a -> NameMap n b

-- | Looking up a name should always succeed.
--   
--   Note that since <a>Name</a> is <a>Sinkable</a>, a name of scope
--   <tt>n</tt> can be looked up in a <a>NameMap</a> for scope <tt>l</tt>
--   whenever <tt>l</tt> extends <tt>n</tt>.
lookupName :: forall (n :: S) a. Name n -> NameMap n a -> a

-- | Extending a map with a single mapping.
--   
--   Note that the scope parameter of the result differs from the initial
--   map.
addNameBinder :: forall (n :: S) (l :: S) a. NameBinder n l -> a -> NameMap n a -> NameMap l a

-- | Remove the mapping for a binder, shrinking the map back to the outer
--   scope.
--   
--   This is the inverse of <a>addNameBinder</a>, and is what a type
--   checker wants when it leaves a binder it has entered.
popNameBinder :: forall (n :: S) (l :: S) a. NameBinder n l -> NameMap l a -> NameMap n a

-- | Convert a <a>NameMap</a> of expressions into a <a>Substitution</a>.
nameMapToSubstitution :: forall (i :: S) e (o :: S). NameMap i (e o) -> Substitution e i o

-- | Convert a <a>NameMap</a> of expressions into a <a>Scope</a>.
nameMapToScope :: forall (n :: S) a. NameMap n a -> Scope n

-- | Extend a map with multiple mappings (by repeatedly applying
--   <a>addNameBinder</a>).
--   
--   Note that the input list is expected to have <b>at least</b> the same
--   number of elements as there are binders in the input pattern
--   (generalized binder).
addNameBinders :: forall binder (n :: S) (l :: S) a. CoSinkable binder => binder n l -> [a] -> NameMap n a -> NameMap l a

-- | Extend a map with multiple mappings (by repeatedly applying
--   <a>addNameBinder</a>).
--   
--   Note that the input list is expected to have <b>at least</b> the same
--   number of elements as there are binders in the input name binder list.
--   
--   See also <a>addNameBinders</a> for a generalized version.
addNameBinderList :: forall (n :: S) (l :: S) a. NameBinderList n l -> [a] -> NameMap n a -> NameMap l a

-- | Allocate a fresh binder for each element of a list, binding each
--   element to its binder in the map.
--   
--   The continuation receives the extended scope, the binders in the order
--   of the input list, and the extended map. This is the list-shaped
--   counterpart of <a>withFresh</a>, and saves a caller from threading the
--   scope, the binders, and the map through a recursion by hand.
withFreshNameBinderList :: forall (n :: S) a r. Distinct n => [a] -> Scope n -> NameMap n a -> (forall (l :: S). DExt n l => Scope l -> NameBinderList n l -> NameMap l a -> r) -> r

-- | A version of <a>withFreshNameBinderList</a> that allocates within a
--   given range (see <a>withFreshIn</a>). This is the bulk form of
--   range-guarded allocation: pre-allocating the names of a whole unit at
--   once and allocating them one at a time are the same operation at
--   different granularity, so both extend the scope index faithfully.
--   
--   Fails with <a>error</a> when the range is exhausted.
withFreshNameBinderListIn :: forall (n :: S) a r. Distinct n => NameRange -> [a] -> Scope n -> NameMap n a -> (forall (l :: S). DExt n l => Scope l -> NameBinderList n l -> NameMap l a -> r) -> r

-- | An <i>ordered</i> collection (list) of <a>NameBinder</a>s, that
--   together extend scope <tt>n</tt> to scope <tt>l</tt>.
--   
--   For an unordered version see <a>NameBinders</a>.
data NameBinderList (n :: S) (l :: S)

-- | An empty list of binders keeps the scope as is.
[NameBinderListEmpty] :: forall (n :: S). NameBinderList n n

-- | A non-empty list of binders.
[NameBinderListCons] :: forall (n :: S) (i :: S) (l :: S). NameBinder n i -> NameBinderList i l -> NameBinderList n l

-- | Convert an unordered set of name binders into an ordered list (with
--   some order).
nameBindersList :: forall (n :: S) (l :: S). NameBinders n l -> NameBinderList n l

-- | Collect name binders of a generalized pattern into a name binder list,
--   which can be more easily traversed.
nameBinderListOf :: forall binder (n :: S) (l :: S). CoSinkable binder => binder n l -> NameBinderList n l

-- | Convert an ordered list of name binders into an unordered set.
fromNameBindersList :: forall (n :: S) (l :: S). NameBinderList n l -> NameBinders n l

-- | Add a binder to the end of an (ordered) list of binders.
--   
--   Note that <a>NameBinderListCons</a> adds a binder to the <i>front</i>
--   of the list, which is the outermost position. This adds one to the
--   innermost position instead.
snocNameBinderList :: forall (n :: S) (i :: S) (l :: S). NameBinderList n i -> NameBinder i l -> NameBinderList n l

-- | Concatenate two (ordered) lists of binders, the second extending the
--   scope that the first extends to.
concatNameBinderLists :: forall (n :: S) (i :: S) (l :: S). NameBinderList n i -> NameBinderList i l -> NameBinderList n l

-- | Keep only those binders of a list whose names are in a given set.
--   
--   This is the <i>thinning</i> of a chain of binders, and it is what
--   turns a support into a smaller chain in one step. The alternative,
--   asking <a>unsinkAST</a> at every binder whether the term can do
--   without it, walks the term once per binder, whereas a caller can
--   compute the support once and thin against it.
--   
--   The thinned scope <tt>m</tt> is produced rather than given, because
--   there is nothing to give: a term's relevant scope (see
--   <tt>withRelevantScope</tt>) is a subset of <tt>l</tt> and generally
--   not an extension of <tt>n</tt>, since a term need not use everything
--   already in scope. What comes back is <tt>n</tt> extended by the
--   binders that survived, with <tt>Ext n m</tt> and <tt>Ext m l</tt> to
--   place it between the two.
--   
--   The set is taken as given. For a chain whose binders carry types, or
--   anything else living in the intermediate scopes, the caller has to
--   close the set under whatever those mention before thinning by it,
--   since dropping a binder that a surviving binder's type refers to would
--   leave that type unplaceable. The library cannot do that closure,
--   having no view of what a binder carries.
withThinnedNameBinderList :: forall (n :: S) (l :: S) r. Distinct n => NameSet l -> NameBinderList n l -> (forall (m :: S). (Ext n m, Ext m l, Distinct m) => NameBinderList n m -> r) -> r

-- | Some scopes are extensions of other scopes.
--   
--   <b>Important</b>: this class exists to assist tracking scope
--   extensions for type variables of kind <a>S</a>. Users of the foil are
--   not supposed to implement any instances of <a>Ext</a>.
class ExtEndo n => ExtEndo l => Ext (n :: S) (l :: S)

-- | Evidence that scope <tt>l</tt> extends scope <tt>n</tt>.
data ExtEvidence (n :: S) (l :: S)
[Ext] :: forall (n :: S) (l :: S). Ext n l => ExtEvidence n l

-- | Scopes with distinct names.
--   
--   <b>Important</b>: this class exists to explicitly mark scopes with
--   distinct names. Users of the foil are not supposed to implement any
--   instances of <a>Distinct</a>.
class Distinct (n :: S)

-- | Evidence that scope <tt>n</tt> contains distinct names.
data DistinctEvidence (n :: S)
[Distinct] :: forall (n :: S). Distinct n => DistinctEvidence n

-- | A distinct scope extended with a <a>NameBinder</a> is also distinct.
assertDistinct :: forall (n :: S) pattern (l :: S). (Distinct n, CoSinkable pattern) => pattern n l -> DistinctEvidence l

-- | A distinct scope extended with a <a>NameBinder</a> is also distinct.
assertExt :: forall pattern (n :: S) (l :: S). CoSinkable pattern => pattern n l -> ExtEvidence n l

-- | Scope extensions with distinct names.
type DExt (n :: S) (l :: S) = (Distinct l, Ext n l)

-- | Instances of this typeclass possess the ability to inject names.
--   Usually, this is a variable data constructor.
class InjectName (e :: S -> Type)

-- | Inject names into expressions.
injectName :: forall (n :: S). InjectName e => Name n -> e n


-- | Deterministic stripe assignment for separately checked units.
--   
--   Each unit of a module system allocates its top-level names inside its
--   own reservation (see <a>Control.Monad.Foil.Blocks</a>), and the
--   assignment of reservations has to be <i>deterministic</i>: a unit's
--   declarations are numbered <tt>base</tt>, <tt>base + 1</tt>, and so on
--   in declaration order, whatever else is checked around it. Determinism
--   is what makes raw names cacheable, since a unit checked today and a
--   unit loaded tomorrow then agree name for name. It is also what
--   discharges the trust obligation of <a>checkExtScope</a>.
--   
--   The registry is that assignment: an append-only map from unit names to
--   stripe indices, handing out the next index on first use. A build
--   persists it beside the build products, since a cached artifact
--   survives a change elsewhere in the build exactly when the assignment
--   does not move.
--   
--   Where the stripes lie on the raw-name line is a <a>StripeLayout</a>
--   and a policy of the client. The library is region-agnostic, and the
--   allocator admits negative names.
module Control.Monad.Foil.Registry

-- | A stripe's position in the registry: which run of names a unit draws
--   from. Its own type, so that a stripe index cannot be confused with a
--   name, a count, or an offset.
newtype StripeIndex
StripeIndex :: Int -> StripeIndex

-- | How many names a unit may declare: the width of every stripe a layout
--   hands out. Its own type, so that a size cannot be confused with a
--   name, an index, or a base.
newtype StripeSize
StripeSize :: Int -> StripeSize

-- | Where stripe <tt>i</tt> lies on the raw-name line.
--   
--   The library does not choose: whether stripes descend below zero,
--   ascend from some base, or interleave with other reservations is a
--   policy of the client, and everything in
--   <a>Control.Monad.Foil.Blocks</a> works from the resulting
--   <a>NameRange</a>s alone. A layout should give disjoint ranges to
--   distinct indices. Nothing checks this here, but
--   <a>withDisjointUnion</a> refuses the overlap at the point where it
--   would do harm.
newtype StripeLayout
StripeLayout :: (StripeIndex -> NameRange) -> StripeLayout
[stripeRange] :: StripeLayout -> StripeIndex -> NameRange

-- | Stripe <tt>i</tt> is the <tt>i</tt>-th run of <tt>size</tt> names
--   below zero, counting downwards, so stripe 0 is <tt>[-size .. -1]</tt>.
--   Within a stripe, allocation still ascends (see <a>withFreshIn</a>), so
--   declaration order is ascending name order.
--   
--   This layout leaves the whole non-negative range free for a client's
--   local names.
--   
--   <pre>
--   &gt;&gt;&gt; stripeRange (stripesBelowZero (StripeSize 100)) (StripeIndex 0)
--   NameRange {nameRangeLo = -100, nameRangeHi = -1}
--   
--   &gt;&gt;&gt; stripeRange (stripesBelowZero (StripeSize 100)) (StripeIndex 2)
--   NameRange {nameRangeLo = -300, nameRangeHi = -201}
--   </pre>
stripesBelowZero :: StripeSize -> StripeLayout

-- | Stripe <tt>i</tt> is the <tt>i</tt>-th run of <tt>size</tt> names at
--   or above a base, counting upwards, so stripe 0 is <tt>[base .. base +
--   size - 1]</tt>.
--   
--   <pre>
--   &gt;&gt;&gt; stripeRange (stripesAbove 0 (StripeSize 100)) (StripeIndex 1)
--   NameRange {nameRangeLo = 100, nameRangeHi = 199}
--   </pre>
stripesAbove :: RawName -> StripeSize -> StripeLayout

-- | How far apart consecutive local-region floors sit within a unit's
--   runs. This is spacing, not a hard width: a run is open-ended above its
--   floor, and a scope-driven allocator would have to hold this many names
--   /in scope at once/ to reach the next floor.
newtype RegionWidth
RegionWidth :: Int -> RegionWidth

-- | How many runs of local names a unit may hold before its runs would
--   spill into the next unit's. A spill is not unsound for a client that
--   refreshes on clash. It only forfeits the disjointness described under
--   <a>RegionLayout</a> for the runs past the cap.
newtype RegionsPerUnit
RegionsPerUnit :: Int -> RegionsPerUnit

-- | Where a unit's runs of <i>local</i> names lie: one open-ended region
--   per declaration (or command) of the unit, advanced with
--   <a>nextRegion</a> as the unit's declarations are processed.
--   
--   Stripes make a unit's top-level names disjoint from every other
--   unit's, and runs of local regions do the same for the names a checker
--   invents <i>inside</i> a declaration. A term stored under one
--   declaration then never collides with another declaration's live locals
--   when it is reopened, so a refreshing substitution takes its no-rename
--   fast path throughout.
--   
--   The first run is derived from the unit's stripe index rather than from
--   a counter shared across units, so a unit's elaboration depends only on
--   the unit itself and editing a neighbour moves no name. That is the
--   determinism a cache rests on.
--   
--   The trade-off is that local names carry large offsets. A client that
--   shows raw indices directly may prefer a single flat region, and accept
--   the transient renames instead.
data RegionLayout
RegionLayout :: (StripeIndex -> NameRange) -> (NameRange -> NameRange) -> RegionLayout

-- | The run of the unit's first declaration.
[firstRegionOf] :: RegionLayout -> StripeIndex -> NameRange

-- | The next declaration's run.
[nextRegion] :: RegionLayout -> NameRange -> NameRange

-- | Runs ascending from a base: the unit with stripe index <tt>i</tt>
--   starts its runs at <tt>base + i * perUnit * width</tt>, and each
--   declaration's floor sits <tt>width</tt> above the previous one. The
--   top of every run is open.
--   
--   <pre>
--   &gt;&gt;&gt; let locals = regionsAbove 0 (RegionsPerUnit 0x10) (RegionWidth 0x100)
--   
--   &gt;&gt;&gt; nameRangeLo (firstRegionOf locals (StripeIndex 2))
--   8192
--   
--   &gt;&gt;&gt; nameRangeLo (nextRegion locals (firstRegionOf locals (StripeIndex 2)))
--   8448
--   </pre>
regionsAbove :: RawName -> RegionsPerUnit -> RegionWidth -> RegionLayout

-- | Which stripe each unit's declarations live in, by the unit's name.
--   
--   Append-only: a name, once registered, keeps its stripe for the
--   lifetime of the registry, and the next stripe index is always the
--   registry's size.
type Registry name = Map name StripeIndex

-- | The registry before any unit has ever been checked.
emptyRegistry :: Registry name

-- | How many units have been registered, which is also the next free
--   stripe.
registrySize :: Registry name -> Int

-- | The stripe index of a unit, assigning the next one on first use.
--   
--   Registration hands out the index and not a range. A unit's index
--   determines <i>every</i> reservation derived for it: its stripe under a
--   <a>StripeLayout</a>, and its runs of local names under a
--   <a>RegionLayout</a>. The layouts interpret the index, rather than
--   being consulted here.
--   
--   <pre>
--   &gt;&gt;&gt; let layout = stripesBelowZero (StripeSize 10)
--   
--   &gt;&gt;&gt; let (r1, iA) = registerUnit "A" emptyRegistry
--   
--   &gt;&gt;&gt; stripeRange layout iA
--   NameRange {nameRangeLo = -10, nameRangeHi = -1}
--   
--   &gt;&gt;&gt; stripeRange layout (snd (registerUnit "B" r1))
--   NameRange {nameRangeLo = -20, nameRangeHi = -11}
--   </pre>
--   
--   Registration is idempotent, which is the determinism a cache rests on:
--   
--   <pre>
--   &gt;&gt;&gt; snd (registerUnit "A" r1) == iA
--   True
--   </pre>
registerUnit :: Ord name => name -> Registry name -> (Registry name, StripeIndex)
instance Data.Binary.Class.Binary Control.Monad.Foil.Registry.StripeIndex
instance GHC.Classes.Eq Control.Monad.Foil.Registry.RegionWidth
instance GHC.Classes.Eq Control.Monad.Foil.Registry.RegionsPerUnit
instance GHC.Classes.Eq Control.Monad.Foil.Registry.StripeIndex
instance GHC.Classes.Eq Control.Monad.Foil.Registry.StripeSize
instance GHC.Classes.Ord Control.Monad.Foil.Registry.RegionWidth
instance GHC.Classes.Ord Control.Monad.Foil.Registry.RegionsPerUnit
instance GHC.Classes.Ord Control.Monad.Foil.Registry.StripeIndex
instance GHC.Classes.Ord Control.Monad.Foil.Registry.StripeSize
instance GHC.Internal.Read.Read Control.Monad.Foil.Registry.RegionWidth
instance GHC.Internal.Read.Read Control.Monad.Foil.Registry.RegionsPerUnit
instance GHC.Internal.Read.Read Control.Monad.Foil.Registry.StripeIndex
instance GHC.Internal.Read.Read Control.Monad.Foil.Registry.StripeSize
instance GHC.Internal.Show.Show Control.Monad.Foil.Registry.RegionWidth
instance GHC.Internal.Show.Show Control.Monad.Foil.Registry.RegionsPerUnit
instance GHC.Internal.Show.Show Control.Monad.Foil.Registry.StripeIndex
instance GHC.Internal.Show.Show Control.Monad.Foil.Registry.StripeSize

module Control.Monad.Foil.Relative

-- | Relative monads, restricted to types indexed by scopes in kind
--   <a>S</a>.
class RelMonad (f :: S -> Type) (m :: S -> Type)

-- | Relative version of <a>return</a>.
rreturn :: forall (a :: S). RelMonad f m => f a -> m a

-- | Relative version of <a>&gt;&gt;=</a>.
--   
--   Note the two special additions to the usual definition of a relative
--   binding operation:
--   
--   <ol>
--   <li><tt><a>Scope</a> b</tt> is added since is corresponds to the
--   runtime counterpart of the type parameter <tt>b</tt>.</li>
--   <li><tt><a>Distinct</a> b</tt> constraint helps to ensure we only work
--   with scopes that are distinct.</li>
--   </ol>
--   
--   Technically, it is also possible add similar components for <tt>a</tt>
--   parameter. Also, we could probably treat types in <a>S</a> as
--   singletons and extract distinct scopes that way, preserving the more
--   general type signature for <a>rbind</a>.
rbind :: forall (b :: S) (a :: S). (RelMonad f m, Distinct b) => Scope b -> m a -> (f a -> m b) -> m b

-- | Relative version of <tt>liftM</tt> (an <a>fmap</a> restricted to
--   <a>Monad</a>).
liftRM :: forall f m (b :: S) (a :: S). (RelMonad f m, Distinct b) => Scope b -> (f a -> f b) -> m a -> m b


-- | Example implementation of untyped &lt;math&gt;-calculus with the foil.
module Control.Monad.Foil.Example

-- | Untyped &lt;math&gt;-terms in scope <tt>n</tt>.
data Expr (n :: S)

-- | Variables are names in scope <tt>n</tt>: &lt;math&gt;
[VarE] :: forall (n :: S). Name n -> Expr n

-- | Application of one term to another: &lt;math&gt;
[AppE] :: forall (n :: S). Expr n -> Expr n -> Expr n

-- | &lt;math&gt;-abstraction introduces a binder and a term in an extended
--   scope: &lt;math&gt;
[LamE] :: forall (n :: S) (l :: S). NameBinder n l -> Expr l -> Expr n

-- | Substitution for untyped &lt;math&gt;-terms. The foil helps implement
--   this function without forgetting scope extensions and renaming.
substitute :: forall (o :: S) (i :: S). Distinct o => Scope o -> Substitution Expr i o -> Expr i -> Expr o

-- | Compute weak head normal form (WHNF) of a &lt;math&gt;-term.
--   
--   <pre>
--   &gt;&gt;&gt; whnf emptyScope (AppE (churchN 2) (churchN 2))
--   λx1. (λx0. λx1. (x0 (x0 x1)) (λx0. λx1. (x0 (x0 x1)) x1))
--   </pre>
whnf :: forall (n :: S). Distinct n => Scope n -> Expr n -> Expr n

-- | Compute weak head normal form (WHNF) of a <b>closed</b>
--   &lt;math&gt;-term.
--   
--   <pre>
--   &gt;&gt;&gt; whnf' (AppE (churchN 2) (churchN 2))
--   λx1. (λx0. λx1. (x0 (x0 x1)) (λx0. λx1. (x0 (x0 x1)) x1))
--   </pre>
whnf' :: Expr 'VoidS -> Expr 'VoidS

-- | Compute normal form (NF) of a &lt;math&gt;-term.
--   
--   <pre>
--   &gt;&gt;&gt; nf emptyScope (AppE (churchN 2) (churchN 2))
--   λx1. λx2. (x1 (x1 (x1 (x1 x2))))
--   </pre>
nf :: forall (n :: S). Distinct n => Scope n -> Expr n -> Expr n

-- | Compute normal form (NF) of a <b>closed</b> &lt;math&gt;-term.
--   
--   <pre>
--   &gt;&gt;&gt; nf' (AppE (churchN 2) (churchN 2))
--   λx1. λx2. (x1 (x1 (x1 (x1 x2))))
--   </pre>
nf' :: Expr 'VoidS -> Expr 'VoidS

-- | Pretty print a name.
ppName :: forall (n :: S). Name n -> String

-- | Pretty-print a &lt;math&gt;-term.
--   
--   <pre>
--   &gt;&gt;&gt; ppExpr (churchN 3)
--   "\955x0. \955x1. (x0 (x0 (x0 x1)))"
--   </pre>
ppExpr :: forall (n :: S). Expr n -> String

-- | A helper for constructing &lt;math&gt;-abstractions.
lam :: forall (n :: S). Distinct n => Scope n -> (forall (l :: S). DExt n l => Scope l -> NameBinder n l -> Expr l) -> Expr n

-- | Church-encoding of a natural number &lt;math&gt;.
--   
--   <pre>
--   &gt;&gt;&gt; churchN 0
--   λx0. λx1. x1
--   </pre>
--   
--   <pre>
--   &gt;&gt;&gt; churchN 3
--   λx0. λx1. (x0 (x0 (x0 x1)))
--   </pre>
churchN :: Int -> Expr 'VoidS
instance Control.Monad.Foil.Internal.InjectName Control.Monad.Foil.Example.Expr
instance Control.DeepSeq.NFData (Control.Monad.Foil.Example.Expr l)
instance Control.Monad.Foil.Relative.RelMonad Control.Monad.Foil.Internal.Name Control.Monad.Foil.Example.Expr
instance GHC.Internal.Show.Show (Control.Monad.Foil.Example.Expr n)
instance Control.Monad.Foil.Internal.Sinkable Control.Monad.Foil.Example.Expr

peelConT :: Type -> Maybe (Name, [Type])
unpeelConT :: Name -> [Type] -> Type
pattern PeelConT :: Name -> [Type] -> Type
tvarName :: TyVarBndr a -> Name
removeName :: VarBangType -> BangType

-- | Generate a function to extend scope with variables from a given
--   pattern.
mkExtendScopeFoilPattern :: Name -> Name -> Q [Dec]

-- | Generate a function to extend scope with variables from a given
--   pattern.
mkWithRefreshedFoilPattern :: Name -> Name -> Q [Dec]

-- | Generate a conversion function from raw terms to scope-safe terms.
mkToFoilTerm :: Name -> Name -> Name -> Name -> Q [Dec]

-- | Generate a conversion function from raw terms to scope-safe terms.
mkToFoilPattern :: Name -> Name -> Q [Dec]

module Control.Monad.Foil.TH.MkInstancesFoil

-- | Generate <a>Sinkable</a> and <a>CoSinkable</a> instances.
mkInstancesFoil :: Name -> Name -> Name -> Name -> Q [Dec]

-- | Generate <a>Sinkable</a> and <a>CoSinkable</a> instances.
deriveCoSinkable :: Name -> Name -> Q [Dec]

-- | Generate a structural <a>UnifiablePattern</a> instance, comparing
--   constructors and non-binding fields rather than only the binders.
--   
--   This deriver does not work and has no call sites. See the deprecation
--   note.

-- | <i>Deprecated: This deriver does not work and has no call sites. It
--   reifies the raw (BNFC) pattern type and guesses the scope-safe type
--   and constructor names by prefixing <a>Foil</a>, and it rejects GADT
--   constructors -- so it cannot handle the pattern types that
--   mkFoilPattern and mkFreeFoil generate, nor a hand-written pattern
--   GADT. Instead, derive GenericK and take an empty instance (see
--   Control.Monad.Foil), or write the instance by hand as
--   Language.LambdaPi.Impl.Foil does. Note that the empty instance
--   compares only the binders; see UnifiablePattern. Structural derivation
--   is tracked in <a>https://github.com/fizruk/free-foil/issues/23</a>. To
--   be removed in the next major release.</i>
deriveUnifiablePattern :: Name -> Name -> Q [Dec]
